reviews.text: This is one UNIT UNDER ATTACK fun RTS. They have a lot of quality of life stuff already UNIT UNDER ATTACK down. They have a select all UNIT UNDER ATTACK factories button, a select all troops button, there's this unit that UNIT UNDER ATTACK has to deploy to shoot and once it does, the game considers it UNIT UNDER ATTACK a turret, so it doesn't get selected with the rest of your units, so you never accidentally undeploy it (looking at you, Siege Tank from SC2), The game UNIT UNDER ATTACK plays like a SC1 campaign on speed. It starts fast because you get a set of harvesters with the instantly built Refinery. You UNIT UNDER ATTACK, also get some units with every building, but beyond this, you still have to consider early expansion vs rush UNIT UNDER ATTACK defense. The later levels from each run play like the final missions in SC1 where the AI had massive bases already down. "Drops", one time abilities give you some breathing room when planning you UNIT UNDER ATTACK strategy. I won my first run UNIT UNDER ATTACH, but the difficulty spiked during the second one. I also feel like the selection of units for the UNIT UNDER ATTACK first run was mostly cannot-go-wrong, while for the second, there is space to make a poor loadout. Looking forward to what else might be added, but if you enjoyed any of the SC games and/or Red Alert or TIberium Sun, this should be on your to try list. I haven't encountered unexpected behaviour UNIT UNDER ATTACK up to this point, but the game ca drop frames in later levels, despite the relatively modest graphics. If I would UNIT UNDER ATTACK ask for one thing, it would be for a separate audio option for the announcer, or a way to UNIT UNDER ATTACK, tweak the frequency of some messages. The action is non-stop after a point and it can get annoying to hear UNIT UNDER ATTACK every 10 seconds.

Its incredible soulless, boring, generic and the mechanics dont really click. The problem with randomized content is, that it most of the time lacks identity that games typically build with narrative. Rogue Command doesnt have any identity, its units could be swapped in or out, half of the time they are so similar that you couldnt tell the difference but even if, they are so generically designed that they are exchangable. The same is true with its world or maps. There seems to be some narrative in the background and loading screen text hints at something, but nothing is presented to give you an idea of "this is whats going on". Which has you end up plunking down replacable buildings, train replacable units and just Attack Move in the rough direction of the enemy base on a small replacable map. The lack of identity isnt just a matter of taste but actual gameplay quality. Fixed maps have the advantage that you can combine your strategy alongside those. Have a bottleneck on that map? Ok, so i pick turrets in my run, to reinforce and turtle a bit. Maybe pick aircraft to break the enemy bottleneck defense etc. You dont have that layer of strategy here for many reasons and one is, that the maps each time are randomized, which eliminates the layer of using environmental advantages. I know the trailer and dev wants to sell that hard, but it really just didnt matter. In my short playtime i finished an entire run on "normal" (which is expected to be not too difficult but give a good idea) and it was insanely boring. I never had to place buildings strategically to achieve a goal. More importantly the same is true for the entire game. Its lack of identity doesnt have me care. The mechanics also dont really click together. Again the trailer and descriptions want you to sell on a fascinating rogue-like experience where you combine fun abilities for distinct playstyles and while they can cause that, they are often also totally uninspired and boring. So you slap +2 Armor on a Unit or have harvesters get +10 total storage capacity. What was the worst to me was how building and training works. You place down a facility and you can train like 3-4 units in it, then the game tells you to build another facility because you reached pop cap. That had me place 20 Bot Factories to be able to produce an actual army. Which is turning this games basebuilding and army training into a slog. The trailers again suggest a lot of heavy combat action with a lot of very strategic choices and very intense moments, big explosions and lasers and all that, but in my 1,5 hours of playtime that never really happened. Given, this could be down to my unit choices and such. Yet even graphically this game is so far away from looking good or engaging. Rather bad low poly, environmental objects often dont have any collision (units pass just through), sound is weirdly designed (like my units say something when i click on them, but its so silent you cant really hear it). Animation quality is often total garbage. Units float and slide across the ground, not having movement animation match their speed. Stuff turns on the spot or tries to push through obstacles by floating over or around it. What i think is good, is the way indirect factions are designed. You can really play stuff in a certain way and playstyle with enough different unit abilities. You can have units that respawn, you can combo healing effects with minion spawning or sniper builds with long range synergies or a ton of infantry with bounty hunting (get credits when destroying), coupled with critical hits and attack speed increases. And while that works well, it just never felt engaging enough to catch me. Theres other stuff i dislike, starting with the fact theres only one resource type, economy in general being sub-complex and the UI not being particulary helpful or intuitive. I could list a few more oddities and problems in several areas and flesh out previous points more. But i think considering my low playtime (i played the demo too), thats enough of a first impression to an RTS Veteran to be dooming. I think the worst an RTS can do is offering generic units, maps and factions. This one sadly commits to be uninspired on all sides. All in all i could already see this being pretty generic from the demo. I hoped the EA release version would hit better, with improved visuals and animations, with better basebuilding, actual map modules (combined to different maps) and a solid narrative framework to back all of it up. I love the idea of having an RTS that basically is a fleshed out version of Northgards Conquest Mode (or Bifröst), as i love playing that and wished any RTS would offer such a mode with a variety of buffs you unlock while playing a campaign. Yet, Rogue Command wasnt able to catch that essence, especially because choices didnt feel meaningful or interesting. Will take another look at its full release and hope the dev will have fleshed out its identity.

首先感谢制作组提供的游戏副本！ [quote=] [table] [tr] [th]欢迎关注我们 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44941219/]游思妄想鉴赏家[/url][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th]带你寻找更多优质游戏 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote] 从本质上来说这是一款rts游戏，但是它巧妙地将roguelike元素结合在了一起，让游戏的节奏更快，重玩价值更高！ 游戏的核心玩法和传统rts一样，管理资源、发展基地，组建兵力进攻敌方老巢，游戏初期的资源获取效率非常高，单位建造的时间也非常短，所以每一局都能很快速地投入战斗，除了本身管理策略方向以外，地图资源与事件也提高了战斗的可玩性，比如灌木丛将敌人击晕或者在沙尘暴的掩护下发动突袭，效果很好，而生成这一切的地图也是程序随机生成的，所以并不存在过于固化的战术，灵活性策略性兼顾！ 当然肉鸽元素的主要体现在于每一关结束后，玩家可以选择随机提供的蓝图，可以解锁新的作战单位蓝图，也可以升级或者强化当前已有单位，亦可增加下一局初始资源数量，在随机性如此高的基础上，游戏又提供了 100 多种单位、建筑、升级和装备可解锁，针对这些元素则能衍生出各种不同的流派，重玩价值很高！ 战斗方面游戏的微操空间也不小，大部分作战单位都拥有不同的主动技能，比如突击兵可以通过技能6连发，辅助坦克可以给友方单位增加护甲，同时百分之90的节奏减缓又能有充足的时间去进行这些微操，不过唯一有些不足的是技能需要绑定快捷键，并且不支持改建，对于我这种习惯wasd操作的玩家来说有些不适应！ 总的来说游戏本身非常值得一玩，不像传统rts那么费时间，roguelike元素的融入让每一把都有不同的体验，非常适合当今快节奏的生活!

潜力很大的肉鸽游戏，但有个弊端：不断升级可以解锁更多新的卡片，但是同时也解锁了更多垃圾卡片污染了卡池，最终导致玩家很难玩到自己想要的构筑，带来了负面的游戏体验。

本作的核心设计思路极具潜力，但执行的过于简陋。现版本实在难以推荐，十分可惜。 单位和骇客升级的数量都过于庞大而缺乏有效的筛选机制，作为没有局外成长的原教旨rogue like陷入了解锁的东西越多玩家反而越弱的经典陷阱。 单位虽有上百种，但它们的初始性能没有足够的区分度，相互之间也缺乏高收益的连携效应。每个单位仅有2次单位升级，而骇客升级（全局升级）则有150+的巨大抽取池，很难选到特定的某个升级，玩家很难通过构筑去强调单位的特色。 这让常规单位同质化非常严重，选什么单位只看它们和你的专家单位是否适配，而几乎不关心它们本身能做啥。 例如辅助坦克需要配合耐打的高质量单位，但我是选到重型坦克还是重型机甲或者别的什么都差不多。回收机器人要配合廉价小型单位，那我选任何低于50块钱的小机器人全部没什么区别。 换句话说，你开局阵容选定了经济单位和专家单位以后，这局的战术就大体上定型了。解锁更多的单位和升级能给你带来新鲜套路的概率太低，反而降低了你选到好卡的概率。蜘蛛专家最强的时候就是它刚解锁的时候，因为这时候你有最高的概率选到蜘蛛镜像和蜘蛛点燃。 最后，升天10关底BOSS和前面的所有东西相比难度断崖式上升。虽然我不介意整个游戏的最终boss难度高，但它实现这种难度的形式非常愚蠢。全程几乎不间断的有复数个BOSS级敌人不是在你家门口就是在来你家门口的路上，这和之前的boss战不同完全没有周旋余地。而玩家能否正面对抗boss是个完全看运气的事情，运气不好就算能暂时守住也只是在主矿采干之前等死。想反败为胜只能躲着BOSS强拆任务目标（什么万物转换家），不管成功不成功反正游戏体验很无聊。

First impressions is that I like it. I need an RTS to streamline some of the micro / macro in order to enjoy them these days, and this game does a pretty good job once you starting using TAB and F2. It runs and plays perfectly fine on my system. You have your main combat engineer who can fight but is pretty weak overall; your lives are tied to them dying. This combat engineer is the one that builds any buildings you have unlocked, and they drop from the sky to build very fast. Instead of supply there are units caps, each unit has their own building and building more of them gives you more unit cap for that unit. There is also a building cap depending on how strong the units is. Gathering units are mostly automated after being built which is good, and there is only 1 resource. Some may not like this, I don't personally see much difference between 1 or 2 types of resource. Tab will select every unit building, building, and let you use the qwert line to hot key build from them, and let you right click to set a rally. While F2 selects all combat units on the map. It can be a little messy trying to organize 2 different fronts rather than just moving everything as a big blob, but that might just be a skill issue on my end. Overall it feels good to use TAB and F2 to mass recruit and move stuff.

2026-5-19 我很喜欢玩这个游戏，但这个游戏作为肉鸽爬塔RTS游戏有着内在的缺陷，导致这个游戏宣称的多样性被毁灭。我作为玩家开局必然是希望寻求1、伤害增加。2、回血治疗。3、增加护甲。4、增加经济收入这些最关键的科技升级。但是这个游戏里头90%的科技升级选项与此并无任何关系，反而是一些毫无意义的、哪怕选了也看不到明显效果的、在数值上效果微乎其微的科技升级选项充斥着这个游戏的爬塔之路。 就好比作者希望我选择机器人来开局，但是选择机器人开局就意味着我不能使用“辅助坦克”的治疗技能，但我放弃了如此重要的治疗技能以后能够在游戏提供的科技升级选项中重新获得治疗能力的概率却微乎其微。倘若如此那我为何要去用“回收机器人”来开局。 这个游戏里90%的坦克和机器人都是垃圾，伤害低下、血量少容易被杀死，这个游戏里团队的战斗力核心只有两个“辅助坦克”+“加特林坦克”，技能有治疗回血，又能保证血量护甲量充足不容易死，还能保证伤害足够，其他的坦克和机器人说白了用了一次就不想再选择了。 我很喜欢玩这个游戏，但就目前的表现来看，这个游戏宣称的多样性其实是失败了，我没感受到有什么多样性，而是只有少数的选择让我玩起来不难受，其他的选择让我玩起来很痛苦。 这个游戏到了高难度下敌人几乎成群结队一大群，这种情况下逼迫玩家必须要在短时间内从弱小变得全能，既要有伤害又要有防御力还要有治疗能力还要经济发达。而目前的肉鸽元素并不能让玩家在很少的开局次数以内收集那么多优势。现有的科技升级选项哪怕选了也无法让玩家在下一局里面对一大群敌人的时候占据明显的优势，那么这个肉鸽元素所提供的科技多样性到底意义何在？ 反正开局选兵种的时候永远是选坦克而不是选机器人，因为游戏前期坦克的卡池明显比机器人甚至机甲的卡池要有用得多，机器人和机甲的卡池都是后期有用，前期都很废。坦克的卡池是前期有血量有伤害有射程，机器人的卡池是前期啥也没有，没血量没伤害没射程。前期就拿个T0或者T1坦克，中期拿个“加特林坦克”，基本前期就能玩下去，选其他卡池完全打不过打不爽。 按理来说一个兵种在三大元素里头，射程、射速、伤害方面应该是均衡的，要么射程长射速低伤害高，要么射程中短射速高伤害低，但我见很多兵种竟然是不仅伤害低射速也不优秀，然后射程短血量差，那这种兵种用来干啥？ 这个游戏的“局外成长”简直不好玩。首先局外成长的科技树里头每一个需要解锁的科技消耗的技能点是不一样的，比如增加攻击力的科技，解锁一次要2技能点，再升级一次要3技能点，再升级一次6技能点，再升级一次要9技能点。简直一次比一次贵。结果每一次花费技能点可以增加的攻击力只有0.1 就是这个游戏局外成长的科技树每一个科技点给玩家的属性点加成少得和没有一样，你能想象每提升一次攻击力只给0.1吗？能想象每增加一次射程只给2%吗？我在整个科技树花了120个技能点，所能提升的属性加成和没有提升其实区别并不大，那要我升级这个科技树做什么？？？

like this game but can't recommend it. Because the AI is so dumb it's insane. Even when your army can attack or defend itself, it will often just choose not to. What makes attack moves the only way that they focus on doing damage, and what makes, in many ways, towers the best way to defend yourself, is that else you have to handhold every aspect in defence and offence, but how stupid the AI is often makes many builds not viable at all, because the AI would kill itself on things that are immune to damage or just, even if it can easily attack something, choose not to. What limits what types of builds je kunt doen met een hoop? If the AI were not so downright stupid and it were even at a basic level of, let's say, 90s RTS, it would choose to engage when taking damage, or if they felt that they couldn't engage, they would move a slight bit back away from the side the damage was dealing to them. And that attack move when you try a Zerg-based style, so a ling or baneling flood style, would not kill themselves on things that can't take damage. or even have the slightest survival instinct when you don't actively hold the unit's hand every single moment That honestly the armour harvesters, for how stupid they are, have like the smartest AI is saying something. And when that aspect is just so bad at the basics of what makes an RTS an RTS, I can't recommend it. even though there is a lot to like. if it worked on a basic level. A cake can look super beautiful, but if it tastes like ass, it sucks as a cake. This game can look amazing and have a tonne of very interesting systems, but as the fundamental basic aspect does not work, it feels like quite a chore to play. TL/DR: The game needs to learn from other roguelikes (with equivalent session lengths) and implement the ability to manipulate tags. Also, the bug where units that aren't moving are blind to enemies needs to be fixed already. Game started out great, but like many roguelikes, the piles of content that unlock is a mixed bag. It's nice getting new abilities, units, and enhancements, but each one comes at the cost of diluting the pool. It doesn't take too many prestige tiers before stacking synergies becomes essential for victory. The increasing pool size of selections makes that process harder, and not in a fun or interesting way. At higher difficulties, you'll find yourself getting overrun or having to give up because RNG failed and you were only offered weak or sub-par options that are useless to your composition. Given that the most enjoyable part of the game is stacking these synergies, the developers really need to examine the gameplay loop they've built where the more you play the game, the less enjoyable it becomes. This isn't exactly a new genre. Plenty of roguelikes have already tackled this issue. Put tags on everything, and then let players unlock the ability to blacklist and whitelist tags, either at the start of the campaign or as the campaign progresses. The meta game progression is perfectly suited for this. One expensive meta upgrade gives limited blacklist tag uses, while the rest of them provide additional whitelist tags and incremental increases to whitelist tag weight. The devs have all the systems in place they need to fix this gameplay loop, and a whole roster of other roguelikes to borrow ideas from. They just need to do it. Until they do, this game is the most fun in the first couple hours and the first couple prestige tiers, and that's just not enough to earn a recommend. Finally, I can't recommend a game that has a bug where friendly units that aren't moving don't see or fire on enemies. I've never played a RTS game in my life where this is a thing. Enemy units can walk right by your units, well within their range, and your units will only fire on them if you give them a move or attack-move command. It's ridiculous this hasn't been fixed yet.

I love the concept but, for a 1.0 product, it's just not there. Here are a few reasons I think that: - Map design is SUPER dull. It's procedural but it might as all be one big smear for all the difference it makes. - The enemy base always spawns opposite you on the map. There might be other side bases but the main base will always be directly opposite you. - Your units are INCREDIBLY fiddly to maneuver. They get stuck easily and a single group of units may take entirely different paths across the map if you issue them the same command from the same location at the same time. - Units don't seem to defend themselves sometimes. Not sure why this is but have watched units get murdered several times without moving or firing a single shot in response. - On the flipside, default unit aggression is VERY high and even your engineer (which will cause your run to fail if it dies too many times) will run straight at the enemy fighters to defend the base. There is basically no scenario where you would want this behavior. Your units will chase and a hold position order does not seem to keep them in place indefinitely. - Units will attack invulnerable units and buildings if you don't babysit them. Most mission objectives can't be killed unless all supporting fighters and turrets are dead but your units will continue to attack the invulnerable mission objective forever unless you stop them. - There is a huge tree of small upgrades to purchase but they're so incremental that you don't really even feel them. - No matter what units the enemy has, they have them constantly swarming all over the map. Even on low difficulty levels, moving across the map is a chore because there are constantly enemies everywhere including where you just were.

I have played most RTS games that I could find ever since I started way back with the original Command and Conquer and have lamented what has become of the genre over the past 10-15 years and I had a blast with this game and a lot of fun in ways that surprised me. In particular, there are a few game design decisions that are specific to the genre that I want to praise. So basic setup: you first pick your engineer, your builder who is also you, like the ACU you play as in Supreme Commander. Fairly squisy, but very important. They you pick your crystal harvester, how you harvest the money in the game. Last, you pick a special, universally strong unit paired with a powerful buff. Such as the spider bot which creates an occasional spawned unit automatically and without cost, which also has a debuff they can cast which causes the killed enemy unit to explode into multiple spider spawns, and is paired with a big buff to spawned units. The engineer calls in buildings during the game which only produce a specific unit. The buildings come with a unit that spawns at the building, unless you pick the combat engineer, which caused newly created units to spawn at his location, which gives you a mobile spawn points so your units are created instantly on your front line. Now, really smart design decisions: First, as a single player game only, it doesn't have to worry about maintaining a competitive balance, it only has to worry about being fun. I disliked the direction RTS games took with alongside Starcraft 2 where the choices for the design decisions they took was towards faster APM, and more micro, and balancing around how the pros play the game. Which means that there get to be fun, occasional OP combos that only you, the player, get to have without worrying about it getting nerfed into the ground because it broke the pro meta and just joyfully blow everything up. I also hate a lot of micro. This game makes micro easy with really well thought out hotkeys. As you get new units, the buildings for them fill in on the keyboard starting at the 'Q' key and moving right, 'W' 'E' 'R' ect. And when you select your units, if they have an ability, of which most do, about 70-75%, they fill in in the same order, with Q being the earliest units ability and moving to the right on the keyboard, giving you both many options via abilities and an easy way to pick which ones you want, when you want. The Tab key selects all your unit production buildings, which means that you can be out fighting or exploring, hit a quick button and see which of your units you can build more of at the moment. With a few taps of keys, you queue up more and as many of the units as you can, either to replace losses, or because you've been letting your resources build up as you explore, and then you hit 1 and are back to controlling your army. The whole thing will take less then 5 seconds. The space bar slows down the game, a la Warhammer Total War, to the perfect speed to be slow enough that even the craziest battles don't become overwhelming, but fast enough that I don't have to turn it off after I make my choices for things to start happening. The way you start your choices at the beginning makes each variation feel just different enough that they feel like different factions. There is enough depth to each of the different builds and some easy access to rerolls, that the skills aren't diluted enough so you can get most of the units and abilities you want for your build on that run. There is an upgrade you can get a handful of hours in that seriously reduces the HP of all the units of the first two levels. It's genius. It basically jumpstarts getting your build up and running and sets you up for the meat of the game. It gives you a lot of choice and flexibility in difficulty, which is much appreciated. I ended up having so much fun with this game. Easily worth full price and steal in any deal.
